title: Smooth-curve abelian level rigidification
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $g\geq2$, and $\ell\geq3$ a prime different from $\operatorname{char}(k)$. Use the unpointed smooth moduli groupoid $\mathcal M_{g,0}$ and its abelian level groupoid $\mathcal L_{g,\ell}$ from [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. The groupoid $\mathcal L_{g,\ell}$ is represented by a smooth finite-type $k$-scheme $L_{g,\ell}$. For every $k$-scheme $T$ and every smooth projective geometrically connected genus-$g$ family $X\to T$, the sheaf $\mathcal H_{X/T}$ of that definition is locally constant free of rank $2g$ over $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$, compatibly with arbitrary base change. Its frame functor $T'\mapsto\operatorname{Isom}((\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z)^{2g}_{T'},\mathcal H_{X_{T'}/T'})$ is represented by a finite etale surjective $T$-scheme. Every automorphism of a smooth genus-$g$ family preserving a frame is the identity, and the 2-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal M_{g,0}}L_{g,\ell}$ is naturally equivalent to this discrete frame functor. In particular its objects include an actual isomorphism to $X_{T'}$, not merely equality of coarse moduli points. Finite type, smoothness, finiteness and etaleness use [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Sections 1.1 and 2.3.3--2.3.7, especially Proposition 2.3.4 and Remark 2.3.7; genus g >= 2 throughout. Local PDF WANTED; primary arXiv PDF read online.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-projective-curve-cohomology-local-system] to the test family. The moduli definition supplies smoothness, projective-bundle projectivity and geometric genus $g$; $\ell$ is invertible on every $k$-scheme since it differs from $\operatorname{char}(k)$. Hence $\mathcal H_{X/T}$ has constant rank $2g$ and the specified $\mathrm{BC}^1$ is an isomorphism under every base change.

Apply [lem-sfb-finite-local-system-frame-scheme] to $H=\mathcal H_{X/T}$ and $n=2g$. For each $v:T^\prime\to T$, Step 1 gives the specified isomorphism $\mathrm{BC}^1_v:v^{-1}H\simeq\mathcal H_{X_{T^\prime}/T^\prime}$. Compose a frame of $v^{-1}H$ with $\mathrm{BC}^1_v$; the inverse sends $\alpha$ to $(\mathrm{BC}^1_v)^{-1}\alpha$. These $\mathrm{BC}^1_v$ are compatible with composites $T^{\prime\prime}\to T^\prime\to T$ and with the canonical inverse-image associators by the vertical-pasting compatibility of the exchange map [lemma-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-coherence], so the transport commutes with the restriction maps of both functors. Thus the lemma's universal frame represents exactly the asserted cohomology-frame functor on every $T$-scheme. Its finite etale surjective scheme $P$ and base-change compatibility give the required cover.

Apply [lem-sfb-framed-groupoid-two-fibre] to the smooth moduli groupoid and its cohomology sheaves. Step 1 makes its base-change comparisons invertible; the identity and composition equations hold because $\mathrm{BC}^1$ is compatible with identity squares and with horizontal and vertical pasting [lemma-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-coherence], and $\alpha^*$ is functorial in family isomorphisms with the composite pullback convention of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. The equivalence sends $(Y,\lambda,\phi)$ to $(\phi^*)^{-1}\lambda$ and retains the actual family isomorphism $\phi:Y\simeq X_{T^\prime}$.

The coarse-moduli lemma supplies a smooth finite-type DM stack $\mathcal L_{g,\ell}$ and its coarse scheme $C_{g,\ell}$. Over an algebraically closed field, $u^*\lambda=\lambda$ implies $u^*=\mathrm{id}$ because $\lambda$ is invertible. Step 1 identifies this geometric action with that on $H^1$ of the fibre. Geometric curve-level faithfulness gives $u=\mathrm{id}$. Apply [lem-sfb-inertia-free-coarse-scheme]: the coarse map is an equivalence, $C_{g,\ell}$ is smooth of finite type, and frame-preserving automorphisms over every test scheme are trivial. Set $L_{g,\ell}=C_{g,\ell}$.

Replace $\mathcal L_{g,\ell}$ by its representing scheme in the natural equivalence of Step 3, and use Step 2 to identify its value with $P$. This gives the asserted 2-fibre product and the finite etale surjective frame scheme on every test family. The triviality of frame-preserving family automorphisms is the all-test-schemes conclusion of Step 4. The explicit $\phi$ in Step 3 gives the asserted isomorphism to $X_{T^\prime}$. All constructions use full linear frames, so no choice of a root of unity, rational frame, or symplectic pairing was imposed.

source.place: Section 2.3.3, conclusion and full (not symplectic) abelian level convention.
